==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|avoiden}}, from {{der|en|xno|avoider}}, {{der|en|fro|esvuidier||to empty out}}, from {{m|fro|es-}} + {{m|fro|vuidier}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*vocitāre}} < {{der|en|la-vul|*vocitum}}, ultimately related to {{der|en|la|vacuus}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|forbūgan|lit=to bend away from}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/əˈvɔɪd/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-avoid.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyph|en|avoid}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɔɪd|s=2}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[try]] not to [[meet]] or [[communicate]] with (a person); to [[shun]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To stay out of the way of (something harmful).
#: {{ux|en|I '''avoided''' the slap easily.}}
#: {{ux|en|One town was flooded from the storm, while the other town '''avoided''' the storm.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To keep away from; to [[keep]] [[clear]] of; to stay away from.
#: {{ux|en|I try to '''avoid''' the company of gamblers.}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Comus|page=13|passage=What need a man foreſtall his date of griefe / And run to meet what he would moſt '''avoid'''?}}
#* {{RQ:Macaulay History of England|volume=III|chapter=XIII|page=340|passage=He still hoped that he might be able to win some chiefs who remained neutral; and he carefully '''avoided''' every act which could goad them into open hostility.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=June 19, 2012|author=Phil McNulty|work=BBC Sport
|title=[http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/18181971 England 1-0 Ukraine]
|passage=England could have met world and European champions Spain but that eventuality was '''avoided''' by Sweden's 2-0 win against France, and Rooney's first goal in a major tournament since scoring twice in the 4-2 victory over Croatia in Lisbon at Euro 2004.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To try not to do something or to have something happen.
#* {{RQ:Baldwin Mountain|year_published=1985|part=1|page=20|passage=Then he realized, by the immobility of the other children and by the way they '''avoided''' looking at him, that it was he who was selected for punishment.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To make [[empty]]; to [[clear]].
#* {{circa|1395}}, ''{{w|Wycliffe's Bible|Wycliffe Bible}}'', [https://archive.org/stream/holybiblecontain03wycluoft#page/146/mode/2up Ecclesiasticus 13:6]:
# {{lb|en|transitive|now|_|legal}} To make void, to [[annul]]; to [[refute]] (especially a [[contract]]).
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1395|title={{w|Wycliffe's Bible|Wycliffe Bible}}|section={{w|Epistle to the Galatians|Galatians}} 3:17|url=https://www.studylight.org/desk/index.cgi?rq=47003&t1=en_wyc
|passage=But Y seie, this testament is confermed of God; the lawe that was maad after foure hundrid and thritti yeer, makith not the testament veyn to '''auoide''' awei the biheest.}}
#* {{RQ:Spenser Ireland|page=233|passage={{...}} how can those graunts of the Kings be '''avoyded''', without wronging of those lords, which had those lands and lordships given them?}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|legal}} To [[defeat]] or [[evade]]; to [[invalidate]].
#* {{RQ:Blackstone Commentaries|book=III|chapter=Of Pleading|pages=309–310|pageref=310|text={{...}} in an action for treſpaſſing upon land whereof the plaintiff is ſeiſed, if the defendant ſhews a title to the land by deſcent, and that therefore he had a right to enter, and gives colour to the plaintiff, the plaintiff may either traverſe and totally deny the fact of the deſcent; or he may confeſs and '''avoid''' it, by replying, that true it is that ſuch deſcent happened, but that ſince the deſcent the defendant himſelf demiſed the lands to the plaintiff for term of life.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[emit]] or throw out; to [[void]].
#* {{RQ:d'Anghiera Eden Newe Worlde|chapter=Weste Indies|subchapter=Of the Ilande of Cuba and other|folio=213|verso=1|text={{...}} the citie of ''Memi'' where is a great caue oꝛ denne in the which is a ſpꝛynge oꝛ fountayne that continually '''auoydethe''' a great quantitie of ''Bitumen'' {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Browne Pseudodoxia Epidemica|chapter=Frogges, Toades, and Toad-stone|page=136|text={{...}} a Toad piſſeth not, nor doe they containe thoſe urinary parts which are found in other animals, to '''avoid''' that ſerous excretion; {{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[leave]], [[evacuate]]; to leave as empty, to [[withdraw]] or come away from.
#* {{RQ:Mlry MrtDrthr|12.17|2|X|xvij|passage=Anone they encountred to gyders / and he with the reed shelde smote hym soo hard that he bare hym ouer to the erthe / There with anone came another Knyght of the castel / and he was smyten so sore that he '''auoyded''' his fadel}}
#* '''1565''', {{w|Thomas Stapleton (theologian)|Thomas Stapleton}} (translator), ''{{w|Ecclesiastical History of the English People|The History of the Church of Englande}}. Compiled by {{w|Bede|Venerable Bede}}, Englishman'', Antwerp, Book 5, Chapter 20, pp. 178b-179,<sup>[http://name.umdl.umich.edu/A07396.0001.001]</sup>
#*: {{...}} the bishop commaunded al to '''auoide''' the chambre for an houre, and beganne to talke after this manner to his chaplin {{...}}
#* {{RQ:Holinshed Chronicles|edition=2nd|volume=III|chapter={{w|Henry III of England|Henrie the third}}, the eldest sonne of [[w:John, King of England|king Iohn]]|page=202|column=2|passage=This yeare alſo was a pꝛoclamation made in London, and thꝛoughout all the realme, that all ſtrangers ſhould '''auoid''' the land befoꝛe the feaſt of ſaint Michaell then next following except thoſe that came with merchandize.}}
#* {{RQ:Bacon Sylva Sylvarum|book=New Atlantis|page=8|passage=Wherupon ſixe of vs onely ſtaied, and the reſt '''auoyded''' the Roome.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To get rid of.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1395|title={{w|Wycliffe's Bible|Wycliffe Bible}}|section={{w|First Epistle to the Corinthians|1 Corinthians}} 13:11|url=https://www.studylight.org/desk/index.cgi?rq=45013&t1=en_wyc
|passage=Whanne Y was a litil child, Y spak as a litil child, Y vndurstood as a litil child, Y thouyte as a litil child; but whanne Y was maad a man, Y '''auoidide''' tho thingis that weren of a litil child.}}
#* {{RQ:Holinshed Chronicles|edition=2nd|volume=III|chapter=The oration of {{w|Richard III of England|king Richard the third}} to the chiefteins of his armie|page=756|column=2|passage={{...}} expell out of your thoughts all douts, '''auoid''' out of your minds all feare; and like valiant champions aduance fooꝛth your ſtandards, {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare As You Like It|I|i|page=185|column=1|text={{...}} the ſpirit of my Father, which I thinke is within mee, begins to mutinie againſt this ſeruitude. I will no longer endure it, though yet I know no wiſe remedy how to '''auoid''' it.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[retire]]; to withdraw, [[depart]], [[go away]].
#* {{RQ:Tyndale NT|Matthew|4|8–10|folio=iiij|folioend=iiij|versoend=1|folioref=iiij|versoref=1|text=The devyll {{...}} ſayde vnto hym: all theſe will I geve the / iff thou wilt faull doune and woꝛſhip me. Thẽ ſayde Ieſus vnto hym. '''Avoyd''' Satan.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Coriolanus|IV|v|pages=21–22|pageref=22|text=Pray you poore Gentleman, take vp ſome other ſtation: Heere’s no place for you, pray you '''auoid''': Come.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|1 Samuel|18|11|sig=Dd|page=390|column=2|text=And Saul caſt the iauelin; foꝛ hee ſaid, I will ſmite Dauid euen to the wall with it: and Dauid '''auoided''' out of his pꝛeſence twice.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To become void or vacant.

====Usage notes====
* This is a [[catenative]] verb that takes the gerund ({{m|en|-ing}}). See [[Appendix:English catenative verbs]].

====Synonyms====
* {{sense|to keep away from}} {{see thesaurus|en|avoid}}

====Derived terms====
{{col|en|unavoided|avoidant|avoidless|avoidment|avoid like the plague|avoidable|avoidance|avoider}}
